name: Spot-price / oracle manipulation
requires: a price-consuming path (borrow, mint, liquidate, settle, payout) reachable by an unprivileged caller
a price source that changes within one transaction, such as pool reserves, a live balance, or a single-block TWAP
a fork with the real pool depth and liquidity at the target block
questions: Is the price read from a reserve or balance that any swap changes in the same block, or from a time-weighted accumulator one block cannot move?
What exactly consumes this price (borrow, mint, liquidate, settle, payout), and what is the maximum value that consumer exposes?
If it is a TWAP, what is the window, and can the attacker hold a deviated price for the whole window for less than the profit?
Does the consumer check staleness, round completeness, answer positivity, and a sanity bound on the value?
How much capital moves the pool to the profitable price, and how does that compare with profit plus fees: is a flashloan sufficient?
Is the manipulated reading used to value the attacker's own collateral, or only for an unrelated read?
Can the whole sequence be atomic: borrow, swap, act, unwind, repay?
Is there a second independent price source the consumer also checks, which would cap the manipulation?
false_positives: Uses getReserves or balanceOf but only for a slippage bound or a display value, with no value-bearing consumer
A genuinely long TWAP the attacker cannot fund for the required window
Manipulation cost exceeds the extractable profit at real pool depth
The consumer path is admin-only or unreachable from an unprivileged caller
The price feeds an event or a UI view only
A stale-price claim that used the wrong heartbeat value for that feed
An assumed pool depth that was never measured on the fork
poc_must_show: value extracted in one transaction on a pinned fork block, in a stated unit
the price before and after manipulation plus the cost of the swap (fees and slippage) in the same unit
net profit (extraction minus manipulation cost minus loan fee) strictly positive
the consumer call that converts the moved price into value, with the price-dependent argument named
a control run without the price move showing the same call is unprofitable
capital in versus capital out, with any flashloan demonstrably repaid
impact_bar: Reportable for a single-transaction, self- or flashloan-funded sequence that extracts value because a trusted price was moved, with the net profit quantified. Informational when the price is manipulable but no consumer converts it to value or the manipulation costs more than it yields.
